fields.test_cases_present: partial - the spec defines protocol-compliance RULEs, RECOMMENDATIONs, and waveform sequences that map directly to compliance test scenarios, but does not provide a formal verification plan.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Reset behavior
scenarios: [RST_I] asserted: MASTER [STB_O] and [CYC_O] negated on next rising [CLK_I] (RULE 3.20).
[RST_I] asserted: SLAVE self-starting state machines initialize on next rising [CLK_I] (RULE 3.15).
[RST_I] asserted for >=1 [CLK_I] cycle (RULE 3.05); [RST_I] MAY be held indefinitely (PERMISSION 3.00).
[RST_I] negated: MASTER MAY assert [STB_O] / [CYC_O] starting at the next rising [CLK_I] (OBSERVATION 3.05).

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: CYC_O / STB_O assertion ordering
scenarios: [CYC_O] asserted no later than [STB_O] assertion (RULE 3.25).
[CYC_O] negated no earlier than [STB_O] negation (RULE 3.25).
MASTER MAY assert [CYC_O] indefinitely (PERMISSION 3.05) — but RECOMMENDATION 3.05 advises against this for arbitration.
PERMISSION 3.40: if MASTER does not generate wait states, [STB_O] and [CYC_O] MAY be assigned the same signal.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: SLAVE ignores when CYC_I=0
scenarios: SLAVE MAY NOT respond to any SLAVE signals when [CYC_I] is negated (RULE 3.30).
SLAVE MUST always respond to SYSCON signals (RULE 3.30).

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Standard handshake AND rule
scenarios: [ACK_O], [ERR_O], [RTY_O] generated from logical AND of [CYC_I] AND [STB_I] (RULE 3.35).
PERMISSION 3.10: if SLAVE guarantees no wait state and ERR_I/RTY_I unused, [ACK_O] MAY be tied to (STB_I AND CYC_I).

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: At most one termination signal
scenarios: SLAVE supporting [ERR_O] or [RTY_O] MUST NOT assert more than one of [ACK_O] / [ERR_O] / [RTY_O] at any time (RULE 3.45).

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: STB_O qualification of address/data/control
scenarios: MASTER MUST qualify [ADR_O], [DAT_O], [SEL_O], [WE_O], [TAGN_O] with [STB_O] (RULE 3.60).
All qualified signals MUST be VALID when [STB_O]=1.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: ACK_O / ERR_O / RTY_O qualification of DAT_O
scenarios: SLAVE MUST qualify [DAT_O()] with [ACK_O] / [ERR_O] / [RTY_O] (RULE 3.65).

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Minimum interface signals
scenarios: MASTER MUST include at least [ACK_I], [CLK_I], [CYC_O], [RST_I], [STB_O] (RULE 3.40).
SLAVE MUST include at least [ACK_O], [CLK_I], [CYC_I], [STB_I], [RST_I] (RULE 3.40).

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: MASTER must operate when ACK_I held
scenarios: MASTER MUST be designed to operate normally when SLAVE holds [ACK_I] asserted (RULE 3.55).

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Classic SINGLE READ cycle
scenarios: Sequence per Figure 3-5 (Section 3.2.1) — MASTER drives address+control+CYC_O+STB_O; SLAVE asserts ACK_I with read data; MASTER latches and terminates.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Pipelined SINGLE READ cycle
scenarios: Sequence per Figure 3-6 (Section 3.2.2) — MASTER asserts STB_O once; STALL_I=0 so request accepted; SLAVE asserts ACK_I with data; MASTER terminates with single CYC_O cycle.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Classic SINGLE WRITE cycle
scenarios: Sequence per Figure 3-7 (Section 3.2.3) — MASTER drives address+write-data+WE_O=1+SEL_O+CYC_O+STB_O; SLAVE asserts ACK_I; MASTER terminates.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: BLOCK READ cycle
scenarios: Sequence per Figure 3-10 (Section 3.3.1) — multiple READ phases inside a single CYC_O; MASTER and SLAVE both insert wait states.
Pipelined variant Figure 3-11 — STALL_I causes MASTER to repeat a request.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: BLOCK WRITE cycle
scenarios: Sequence per Figure 3-12 (Section 3.3.2) — multiple WRITE phases inside a single CYC_O.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: RMW (atomic read-then-write) cycle
scenarios: Sequence per Figure 3-14 (Section 3.4) — single CYC_O wrapping READ phase then WRITE phase to same address; SLAVE serves both without releasing arbitration.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: BIG / LITTLE ENDIAN data organization
scenarios: Data organization on 64-bit port (Figure 3-18): BYTE / WORD / DWORD / QWORD ordering matches Section 3.5.3.
Data organization on 32-bit port (Figure 3-19): matches Section 3.5.4.
Data organization on 16-bit port (Figure 3-20): matches Section 3.5.5.
Data organization on 8-bit port (Figure 3-21): BIG and LITTLE ENDIAN identical (port size = granularity).

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Registered Feedback Classic cycle
scenarios: CTI_O=3'b000; behaves as Wishbone Classic; Figure 4-4.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Registered Feedback Constant Address Burst
scenarios: CTI_O=3'b001; ADR_O held constant; multiple beats inside a single CYC_O; End-of-Burst CTI_O=3'b111 on the last beat (Figure 4-8 / 4-9).

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Registered Feedback Incrementing Burst
scenarios: CTI_O=3'b010; BTE_O selects Linear / Wrap-4 / Wrap-8 / Wrap-16; ADR_O increments per data size; End-of-Burst CTI_O=3'b111 on the last beat (Figure 4-10 / 4-11).

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: End-Of-Burst signaling
scenarios: MASTER MUST set CTI_O=3'b111 to signal the end of the current burst (RULE 4.30).
MASTER MAY use End-Of-Burst to indicate a single access (PERMISSION 4.40) — a single access is in fact a burst of length one.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Limited Registered Feedback support
scenarios: MASTER / SLAVE that supports a limited number of burst types MUST complete unsupported cycles as Classic [CTI_IO()=3'b000] (RULE 4.10).
MASTER / SLAVE that supports a limited number of burst extensions MUST complete unsupported cycles as Classic (RULE 4.25).
Permission 4.05: MAY support limited burst types; PERMISSION 4.25: MAY support limited burst extensions.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Registered Feedback core must also support Classic
scenarios: All WISHBONE Registered Feedback compatible cores MUST support WISHBONE Classic bus cycles (RULE 4.00).

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Incrementing burst requirements (RULE 4.40)
scenarios: Same operation (read or write) for all beats.
[SEL_O()] same value for all beats.
[ADR_O()] incremented per the data array size.
Wrap size set by [BTE_O()] signals.

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: Constant address burst requirements (RULE 4.35)
scenarios: Same operation (read or write) for all beats.
[SEL_O()] same value for all beats.
[ADR_O()] same value for all beats (constant).

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: User-defined tag TAG TYPE assignment
scenarios: Every user-defined tag MUST be assigned a TAG TYPE from Table 3-1 (RULE 3.70).
Tag MUST adhere to the timing specifications given for the indicated TAG TYPE.
DATASHEET MUST describe the tag name, TAG TYPE, and operation (RULE 2.15 item 6).

derived_compliance_test_categories.name: INTERCON watchdog escape (RECOMMENDATION 3.10)
scenarios: INTERCON watchdog monitors MASTER [STB_O]; on time-out, INTERCON asserts [ERR_I] or [RTY_I] to escape deadlock.

evidence.quote: All WISHBONE interfaces MUST initialize themselves at the rising [CLK_I] edge following the assertion of [RST_I]. They MUST stay in the initialized state until the rising [CLK_I] edge that follows the negation of [RST_I]. The following MASTER signals MUST be negated at the rising [CLK_I] edge following the assertion of [RST_I]: [STB_O], [CYC_O].

MASTER interfaces MUST assert [CYC_O] for the duration of SINGLE READ / WRITE, BLOCK and RMW cycles. SLAVE interfaces MAY NOT respond to any SLAVE signals when [CYC_I] is negated. The cycle termination signals [ACK_O], [ERR_O], [RTY_O] must be generated in response to the logical AND of [CYC_I] and [STB_I].
RULE 3.75: All MASTER and SLAVE interfaces that support SINGLE READ or SINGLE WRITE cycles MUST conform to the timing requirements given in sections 3.2.1 and 3.2.2 (READ) / 3.2.3 and 3.2.4 (WRITE).
All MASTER and SLAVE interfaces that support BLOCK cycles MUST conform to the timing requirements given in sections 3.3.1 and 3.3.2.
All MASTER and SLAVE interfaces that support RMW cycles MUST conform to the timing requirements given in section 3.4.

All WISHBONE Registered Feedback compatible cores MUST support WISHBONE Classic bus cycles. MASTER and SLAVE that support CTI_I()/CTI_O() MUST support at least Classic [000] and End-of-Cycle [111]. Cores designed for a limited number of burst types MUST complete unsupported cycles as Classic [CTI_IO()='000'].
A MASTER MUST set End-Of-Burst on [CTI_O()] to signal the end of the current burst.
A MASTER signaling an incrementing burst MUST initiate another cycle; same operation, same SEL_O, ADR_O incremented, wrap size set by BTE_O.
A MASTER signaling a constant address burst MUST initiate another cycle; same operation, same SEL_O, same ADR_O.
